attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The firm part is 'will, inevitably, start charging their customers more'. The billing shift and subscription cuts stay under his 'very likely' hedge, so they are not scored. He gave no deadline.

contract.note: Reading 'charging more' as a higher list price or per-token rate on an existing product is ordinary and fair. It is also needed for both companies. Leaving out usage-limit cuts is a cautious choice, not a stretch.

evidence.note: Anthropic paused a billing change and kept limits as they were. That is not a price rise, and with no deadline it does not contradict the forecast.
Shows both companies on the IPO path (Anthropic has filed an S-1; OpenAI expected in early 2027). It says nothing about prices.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet shows no confirmed list-price or per-token rise at either company by the cutoff. Under an open horizon that is not failure, and the early-support rule was not met. So the forecast stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: A present-tense, unhedged statement that AI compute demand outside OpenAI and Anthropic is only a few billion dollars.

contract.note: Reading the claim as 2026 compute spending or commitments by other buyers is ordinary and fits his 2026 framing. The result holds even on a narrower reading that leaves out hyperscaler self-use, because Meta's rental deal with Nebius is third-party demand.

evidence.note: xAI spent $7.72bn on AI capex in Q1 2026 alone, before its May capacity deal with Anthropic. That is far above a few billion a year.
Covers Nebius deals from 2025, which fall outside the 2026 period.
In March 2026 Meta committed $12bn, and up to $27bn, to buy compute from Nebius for its own use.
Meta's Q2 2026 capex was $31bn, but the share spent on AI compute is not broken out.
AMD's release shows Meta buying GPUs at gigawatt scale. It gives no dollar figure.

reviews.rationale: Buyers other than OpenAI and Anthropic show 2026 AI compute demand well above a few billion dollars. xAI spent $7.72bn in one quarter, and Meta signed a $12bn+ compute purchase from Nebius. Either meets the contract's contradiction condition.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: This is an interpretive claim that cost complaints signal AI slowing down. It is unhedged and in the present tense. The underlying assertion, that AI is slowing, is what gets tested.

contract.note: He named no measure. Reading 'slowing down' as slower revenue growth at the main AI sellers is an ordinary reading for this business argument, and the contract ties it to his nearby sentence about revenue growth. The result depends on this reading, as the contract says.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own release: Azure grew 43% year on year in April–June 2026, up from 40% the quarter before.
The comparison quarter: Azure grew 40% in January–March 2026.
Anthropic's Q2 2026 revenue rose 144% on Q1, faster than the quarter before. The source is a summary of the S-1, available before the cutoff.
The quarterly revenue series gives about +132% for Q1, against +144% for Q2.

reviews.rationale: On the contract's fair plain reading, revenue growth at the main AI sellers sped up in Q2 2026 rather than slowing. Azure went from 40% to 43%, and Anthropic's quarter-on-quarter growth went from about 132% to 144%. That meets the contradiction condition.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Calamitously expensive' is a judgment. The testable part is the absolute claim that costs 'have only ever increased' for both providers and customers, set against promises of AI getting cheaper.

contract.note: Because the claim contrasts costs with promises of AI getting cheaper, reading it as unit or per-task prices is the ordinary reading. The contract flags a total-spending reading as an alternative, and the choice affects the result.

evidence.note: OpenAI cut the price of the same o3 model by 80% in June 2025.
Anthropic priced Opus 4.5 at $5/$25 per million tokens, against $15/$75 for Opus 4: a two-thirds cut at the same tier. This is a company pricing disclosure.
A preprint finds per-task cost on ARC-AGI fell about 390x in a year, partly because of less parallel compute.
Anthropic's total compute bill rose from Q1 to Q2 2026. That fits only a total-spending reading, not unit costs.

reviews.rationale: Within the period there are documented price cuts for the same model or tier (o3 down 80%, Opus tier down 67%) and falling per-task costs. These contradict 'only ever increased' for customers, and that alone falsifies the absolute claim. Provider unit costs are not shown in the packet.
